slides.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
slides.tldr: CONTROLLABLE OPINION DYNAMICS IN LLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents to separate belief from speech, enabling controllable and auditable opinion dynamics for social simulations, which supports MIMIC's goal of modeling hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Bayesian Chronicle Agents use an explicit belief layer to make LLM social simulations controllable and auditable.
card.key_idea: A Bayesian update layer separates latent beliefs from LLM-generated speech, using a prior-strength parameter (κ) to control stubbornness and replicate classical opinion dynamics regimes.
card.evaluation: Tested on four LLMs (GPT, Llama, Claude) using synthetic policy questions; validated via Spearman rank-recovery of κ and FJ fixed-point R² (0.93–0.99).
card.limitation: Limited to one synthetic topic, binary stances, and small populations (N=20) on complete graphs; not predictive of real human trajectories.

slides.title: ECHO: A Matched-Contrast Benchmark for Context-Sensitive Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces a diagnostic benchmark to evaluate whether full-duplex systems can distinguish between interruptions and backchannels based on dialogue context, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: ECHO is a diagnostic benchmark for Chinese full-duplex dialogue to evaluate context-sensitive turn-taking decisions.
card.key_idea: It uses matched-contrast pairs where the same user insertion is paired with different dialogue contexts to distinguish between interruptions (Yield) and backchannels/off-talk (Keep).
card.evaluation: Evaluated four speech systems and Gemini (text reference) using Pairwise Action Success Rate (PASR). Results show most systems have a strong Yield bias.
card.limitation: Uses synthesized audio rather than natural speech, and interruption waveforms include label-dependent RMS scaling and onset emphasis.

slides.title: Understanding Engagement and Intrusiveness in Assistive Human-Robot Interaction Using Individual Traits
slides.highlight: This research examines how personality and demographics influence perceptions of robot intrusiveness and engagement, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Individual personality traits and demographics significantly influence perceived robot intrusiveness and interaction dynamics in assistive HRI.
card.key_idea: Compared a reactive, insistent robot (System 1) with a cautious, LLM-driven robot (System 2) to analyze how Big Five traits and demographics modulate user experience.
card.evaluation: User study with 32 participants in a simulated hospital; used Godspeed, SAM, UES, and Big Five Inventory. Results show significant gender and personality effects.
card.limitation: The study used a moderate sample size (32 participants), potentially limiting the generalizability of the findings across different HRI domains.

slides.title: When Should Robots Intervene? Balancing Engagement and Intrusiveness in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research explores how context-aware robot intervention strategies affect user experience and perceived support, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Context-aware robot interventions reduce perceived intrusiveness without compromising perceived intelligence or overall user engagement.
card.key_idea: Comparison of a robot-centric strategy (continuous following and prompting) versus a context-aware strategy (selective interventions based on multimodal cues and task context).
card.evaluation: User study with 32 participants in a simulated hospital; measured via SAM, Godspeed, UES, and Likert scales. Results show significant reduction in intrusiveness.
card.limitation: No dominant user preference emerged, as some users viewed high intrusiveness as supportive companionship in unfamiliar environments.

slides.title: ABM-SIRTEM: A Hybrid Agent-Based and Epidemiological Model for Pandemic Response
slides.highlight: This hybrid model integrates individual-level socioeconomic factors and compliance dynamics with disease spread, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: ABM-SIRTEM is a hybrid model coupling population-level disease dynamics with agent-based socioeconomic behavior and compliance.
card.key_idea: It integrates the SIRTEM epidemiological model with an agent-based model using evolutionary game theory to evolve compliance based on economic productivity, mental well-being, and health risks.
card.evaluation: Calibrated using Bayesian optimization against historical COVID-19 positive/negative test counts from four U.S. states; results broadly reproduce timing of major waves.
card.limitation: The evaluation assesses calibration fit rather than performance on held-out data; negative test counts were substantially underestimated in some states.

slides.title: Audio-Visual Turn-taking Prediction in Cocktail Party Scenarios
slides.highlight: This research evaluates audio-visual predictive turn-taking models in cocktail-party scenarios, providing insights into modality-specific degradation and adaptation in noisy human interactions relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Audio-visual turn-taking models degrade in cocktail-party scenarios but improve via large-scale pre-training and fine-tuning.
card.key_idea: Evaluates Voice Activity Projection (VAP) variants (Audio, Video, Multimodal) on AVCocktail, analyzing generalisation from clean data and the impact of fine-tuning and pre-training scale.
card.evaluation: Tested on Candor and AVCocktail datasets using weighted F1 scores. Results show MM-VAP is most robust, with up to 30% relative improvement after fine-tuning.
card.limitation: Models suffer from catastrophic forgetting of clean domains after adaptation and struggle to effectively fuse noisy audio with visual cues.

slides.title: Gaze as Evidence for Common Grounding: A Cross-Corpus Analysis of MapTask and MUNDEX
slides.tldr: GAZE AS A CUE FOR COMMON GROUNDING
slides.highlight: This research analyzes how gaze features correlate with grounding and reference interpretation in collaborative tasks, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Gaze patterns provide consistent, though modest, evidence of grounding across two different asymmetric collaborative tasks.
card.key_idea: Mapping MapTask and MUNDEX gaze into a shared partner/task/away vocabulary to analyze associations between gaze features (proportions, entropy, transitions) and grounding states.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via Mann-Whitney U tests, GEE, and logistic regression (macro-F1) using grouped cross-validation on MapTask and MUNDEX corpora.
card.limitation: Small effect sizes, limited participant groups, and sensitivity to the unit of inference (dialogue vs. participant).

slides.title: PRISM: Predictive Representation of Interaction Style and Motion for Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: PRISM uses a transformer encoder to infer human interaction traits from passive observations, improving collision rates and navigation efficiency in crowds. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and social robots.

card.one_liner: PRISM improves social robot navigation by passively inferring pedestrian interaction styles from observed trajectories.
card.key_idea: A transformer encoder uses Rank-N-Contrast loss to map trajectories into a continuous ordinal latent space, providing style vectors and temporal confidence scores to the policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in PyBullet simulations using ORCA pedestrians; PRISM reduced collision rates (0.19 to 0.12 in training distribution) compared to the HEIGHT baseline.
card.limitation: Results are limited to synthetic ORCA-based heterogeneity and lack confidence intervals or real-world pedestrian data validation.

slides.title: UniExo: Unified Multi-Skill Policies for Musculoskeletal Locomotion and Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for co-adapting a unified exoskeleton controller with a multi-skill human policy, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI coadaptation and skill acquisition across diverse activities.

card.one_liner: UniExo provides a unified, multi-skill exoskeleton controller supporting diverse locomotor activities and transitions without explicit mode switching.
card.key_idea: Distills four single-skill musculoskeletal experts into one latent-conditioned policy, then co-adapts a hip exoskeleton controller using multi-agent reinforcement learning.
card.evaluation: Simulated tracking (94.7% success) and hardware tests with six participants across four treadmill speeds and a continuous multi-skill route.
card.limitation: Limited to four flat-ground skills; does not measure metabolic cost; simulated exoskeleton assumes rigid attachment and coaxial axes.

slides.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
slides.tldr: DUAL-PROCESS AGENTS WITH MEMORY AND SELF-REFLECTION
slides.highlight: This work introduces an Adaptive Memory Module and a Self-Reflection Module to improve state tracking and corrective intervention, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and self-correction.

card.one_liner: Dual-process language agents improve in interactive environments by combining episodic memory with bounded self-reflection.
card.key_idea: Extends SwiftSage with an Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) for salience-gated episodic storage and a Self-Reflection Module (SRM) for execution-time validation and trigger-based corrective intervention.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ScienceWorld using final score, success rate, and step efficiency. Full system achieved best results (64.62 score, 43.17% success).
card.limitation: Memory is primarily episodic without semantic consolidation; SRM relies on hand-crafted thresholds and shallow deterministic repairs.

slides.authors: João Meneses dos Santos et al.

slides.title: Voice-Light: A Full-Duplex Cascaded Voice Agent with Causal Turn-Taking and Speculative Generation
slides.tldr: FULL-DUPLEX VOICE AGENT WITH CAUSAL TURN-TAKING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a voice agent capable of handling overlap and speculative generation to improve turn-taking. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement in human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: A full-duplex voice agent using speculative generation and a causal adapter for low-latency turn-taking.
card.key_idea: Combines a shared-encoder causal adapter for turn-inference with private speculative response generation and a hybrid controller to manage reversible playback and audible-only conversation history.
card.evaluation: Tested on 1,673 real-conversation candidates and a 36-turn operator case study; learned turn-taking failed to beat Silero timing baselines.
card.limitation: Learned turn-completion performed poorly on real human data compared to synthetic sets; deployment study lacked diverse users and controlled environments.

slides.title: GMO Launches Humanoid Robot Ambulance in Tokyo
slides.highlight: The launch of a humanoid robot ambulance in Tokyo provides a real-world example of embodied AI in public service, relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Chinese Startup Spirit AI Predicts Humanoid Robots Following Verbal Commands by Mid-2027
slides.highlight: Spirit AI anticipates the arrival of humanoid robots capable of following verbal commands by mid-2027, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Designing Against Deskilling: Metacognitive Feedback Reduces Cognitive Offloading to LLM Assistants
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that metacognitive feedback can reduce cognitive offloading to LLM assistants and improve user performance, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition in human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Metacognitive feedback reduces cognitive offloading to LLM assistants and improves subsequent unaided skill performance.
card.key_idea: Comparing metacognitive feedback (making offloading implications explicit) and effort-based rewards (incentivizing less AI help) to prevent deskilling during fraction arithmetic practice.
card.evaluation: Preregistered online experiment (N=704) using a 2x2-plus-control design; measured answer offloading and unaided test performance. Results show metacognitive feedback was effective, rewards were not.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: DiaWhisper-DPO: Role-Attributed Transcription of Clinical Interviews via Failure-Mined Preference Optimization
slides.highlight: This work introduces DiaWhisper-DPO, an end-to-end model for transcription and role attribution in clinical interviews. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on diarization and identity recognition within hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: DiaWhisper-DPO enables end-to-end role-attributed clinical transcription by refining Whisper using failure-mined preference optimization.
card.key_idea: LoRA-tuned Whisper-large-v3 with an auxiliary role head, further refined via DPO using genuine decoding failures as rejected completions and ground truth as chosen completions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DAIC-WOZ and PDCH-HAMD against cascaded baselines; achieved 0.973 role accuracy and 0.119 DER on DAIC-WOZ, showing significant seed stability gains.
card.limitation: Output still requires human verification as incorrect role attribution can distort clinical depression-screening signals.

slides.title: Mental Models in Human-AI Interaction: Methods and Challenges in the Generative and Agentic AI Era
slides.tldr: CRITICAL REASSESSMENT OF MENTAL MODELS IN HUMAN-AI INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This work examines how users reason about and interact with AI systems, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on modeling the state of hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: A workshop proposal to reassess mental model research in the era of generative and agentic AI.
card.key_idea: A theoretical and methodological exchange using lightning talks, peer elicitation exercises, and structured discussions to standardize how mental models are conceptualized and studied in human-AI interaction.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the text describes a proposed workshop program rather than a completed study with results.
card.limitation: The construct is currently operationalized intuitively, lacks commensurability across diverse elicitation methods, and is often blurred with adjacent concepts.

slides.title: Affective Shared Autonomy: Temporal Affect Dynamics and Subjective Evaluation in Bimanual Teleoperation Tasks
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework that modulates robotic assistance based on real-time operator affective states, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: An affect-aware shared autonomy framework for bimanual teleoperation that modulates robotic assistance based on operator states.
card.key_idea: A multimodal fusion model (facial video, cardiac signals, arm kinematics) estimates affective states to trigger assistance only during sustained adverse states, preserving user agency.
card.evaluation: User study (N=30) across three modes. Affect-aware assistance increased productive states by 39.7% and outperformed zero-shot baselines in state tracking accuracy.
card.limitation: Personalized affective models require iterative calibration; time-constrained trials limited the system's ability to fully co-adapt with participants.

slides.title: Design and Experimental Validation of a 3D Printed Torsional Series Elastic Actuator for Safe Human Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: 3D PRINTED COMPLIANT ACTUATOR FOR SAFE pHRI
slides.highlight: This work presents a 3D printed torsional series elastic actuator that ensures intrinsic safety during physical human-robot interaction, supporting the RwB goal of developing safe embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A 3D-printed TPU torsional spring actuator providing low-stiffness compliance for safe human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: A TPU-based 3D printed torsional spring integrated with a hybrid position controller and torque threshold switching to achieve linear torque-deformation and passive damping.
card.evaluation: Validated via FEA and experiments; showed <3% deviation from predictions and successful non-stationary trajectory tracking and disturbance yielding.
card.limitation: FDM structural anisotropy causes slight variance between numerical predictions and experimental results.

slides.title: Beyond "ChatGPT Can Make Mistakes": Designing Interventions to Support Metacognitive Monitoring in AI-Assisted Work
slides.tldr: DESIGNING INTERVENTIONS FOR AI METACOGNITIVE MONITORING
slides.highlight: This research explores a design space for interventions that support metacognitive monitoring in AI-assisted work, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition for human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: A design space and experiment on interventions to improve users' metacognitive monitoring of AI assistance.
card.key_idea: Organizes 30 expert-elicited interventions into a design space based on time (when), level (whose competence), and source (who supplies the cue).
card.evaluation: Between-subjects experiment (N=917) using 12 planning problems; reliability cards and contrasting replies improved monitoring but not task performance.
card.limitation: Interventions generally lowered usability, increased workload, and did not reliably improve actual task accuracy.

slides.authors: Manuel A. D. Santos et al.

slides.title: OpenRoIS: A Community-Driven Open-Source Middleware Implementing the Robotic Interaction Service (RoIS) Framework for Physical Robots and Virtual Agents
slides.highlight: OpenRoIS provides a platform-independent implementation of the RoIS Framework 2.0, allowing service applications to interact with physical robots and virtual agents via standardized interfaces. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: OpenRoIS is an open-source middleware implementing the OMG RoIS 2.0 standard for platform-independent robot interaction.
card.key_idea: A recursive engine architecture using JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSockets, featuring a five-method internal component contract and SDKs for TypeScript, C#, and Python.
card.evaluation: Demonstrated end-to-end with a web application controlling physical robots (Kachaka, Reachy Mini); no formal experimental evaluation provided.
card.limitation: Currently in an early stage with APIs subject to change and lacking latency benchmarks and a full component library.

slides.title: BirdsongChat: A Hybrid Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Embodied Behavior Simulation
slides.tldr: HYBRID MULTI-AGENT FRAMEWORK FOR MULTIMODAL EMBODIED BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that uses a Unified Parameter Representation to bridge semantic reasoning and physical execution for synchronized 3D motion and sound. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

card.one_liner: BirdsongChat uses a hybrid multi-agent framework to simulate synchronized 3D bird motion and soundscapes from multimodal inputs.
card.key_idea: A Unified Parameter Representation (UPR) bridges LLM-based reasoning agents and physically-based simulation agents, mapping semantic intent to interpretable kinematic, acoustic, and environmental parameters.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 90 runs of 18 text/image prompts; achieved 94.4% cross-modal coherence, 100% affective consistency, and 92.6% generation consistency.
card.limitation: Visually complex or ambiguous image prompts can lead to lower cross-modal coherence due to challenges in semantic-to-physical grounding.

slides.title: Dynamic Generalized Gromov-Wasserstein Optimal Transport
slides.highlight: This work introduces a dynamic framework for Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport to preserve spatial structure, which is relevant to the MOSAIC project's use of Optimal Transport for human-AI intent alignment.

card.one_liner: TP-DATE provides a simulation-free framework for dynamic structure-aware optimal transport using travelling-pair flow matching.
card.key_idea: It generalizes Quadratic-form OT (QOT) dynamically by modeling interacting conditional paths (travelling pairs) and marginalizing them into a single vector field via flow matching.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on synthetic and real spatial transcriptomics data; results show better spatial structure preservation and improved continuous 3D dynamics reconstruction.
card.limitation: The dynamic formulation is currently restricted to cases where the start and end spaces are the same.
